edits.new: saw no noticeable blooming from a retroreflector beside a 5% target at 7.2 m, although the retroreflector's measured SNR exceeded that target's by 37.7 dB in the same single acquisition [P, Extended Data Table 2; E: $10\log_{10}(113{,}715/19.4)=37.7$ dB]. The 31.8 dB of "Measured at a lidar wavelength" comes from the same row ($10\log_{10}(113{,}715/74.7)=31.8$ dB against the 50% target). The two differ by 5.9 dB rather than the 10 dB of the reflectance ratio because the paper averages SNR only over returns that gave the correct distance, which favours the strongest speckles of the 5% target, detected in only 17% of acquisitions [P, Methods; E]. Scaled by reflectance from the 50% target, the retroreflector is ≈42 dB above a 5% Lambertian return [E: $31.8+10.0=41.8$ dB].
